item.title: Financial crime has become a major growth industry
item.description: The war may put a damper on bank mergers; and financial crime has become a global industry -- a big global industry

item.title: In stablecoins, banks are confronting the innovator's dilemma
item.description: Noelle Acheson argues that banks' focus on deposit tokens rather than stablecoins is a clear example of the "innovator's dilemma" at work: few economic incentives to embrace the innovation happening at the periphery.

item.title: Zelle ventures into charitable disbursements with Bank of America
item.description: The bank-owned instant payment network has added a new use for its seldom-mentioned disbursement business.

item.title: Fed's Bowman previews streamlined capital framework
item.description: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman outlined upcoming changes to the bank regulatory capital framework in a speech Thursday, focusing on streamlining bank capital requirements through Basel III and global systemically important bank surcharge rules.

item.title: Iran war pushes mortgage rates near yearly high
item.description: The conflict pushed oil price futures above $100 a barrel for a short time earlier this week, which affected bond investors and the 10-year Treasury yield.

item.title: PayPay stock rises by almost 20% after below-range IPO debut
item.description: The payments fintech's Nasdaq debut marks the largest U.S. listing by a Japanese company in a decade and had a strong start despite market turmoil caused by the Iran war.

item.title: Housing bill passes Senate, but window of opportunity narrows
item.description: The Senate passed a bipartisan housing bill in an 89 to 10 vote, but how quickly and easily the bill can pass the House remains unclear.

item.title: Iran names US banks as targets, ratcheting up cyber threat
item.description: A threat that was probabilistic is now official. An Iranian military spokesperson warned of a "painful response" against U.S.-linked banks.

item.title: NY proposal could boost minority banks' access to state deposits
item.description: A New York state bill would reduce the barrier for minority-bank and community-bank participation in the state's long-standing Banking Development District program.

item.title: Esquire makes deal for bigger cut of Chicago's legal market
item.description: The New York-based bank, which serves plaintiff law firms, agreed to pay $348 million for a Windy City community bank.
